title: Signature Harmonizer: runtime orchestrator for OpenAI-style tools vs legacy function calls
creator: Ava Ramirez
description:
Problem: We have two dominant calling surfaces in the wild: OpenAI-style tools (name, description, JSON Schema parameters) and multiple legacy function surfaces used by early adopters (function_name, positional/keyword conventions, inconsistent param casing/enums). Customers are seeing integration breakage when models call tools/functions that differ in naming, parameter shapes, or enum encodings. This causes failed tool invocations, increased error budgets, and heavy support load.

Proposal: Implement a lightweight runtime component (Signature Harmonizer) that normalizes calls at the inference gateway. The Harmonizer will:
- Maintain a canonical registry of tool/function signatures and aliases (per-org and global fallbacks).
- Perform deterministic name normalization (alias mapping, token-based fuzzy match, and explicit alias table) with confidence scoring.
- Translate parameter payloads between representations (e.g., snake_case <-> camelCase, enum label mapping, stringified numbers -> typed values). Use schema-driven translators generated from JSON Schema or function descriptors.
- Provide a safe fallback policy when confidence is low: emit a structured 'tool-call-ambiguous' event instead of calling external tool, surface to SDK with suggested correction and allow automatic retry under opt-in.
- Expose observability: mapping decisions, confidence scores, translation diffs, and audit trail for customer mappings.

Implementation phases:
1) Discovery & collection (2 weeks): instrument logs and ingestion pipeline to collect real tool/function call examples from hosted customers, synthesize common mismatches.
2) Registry & mapping API (2 weeks): design canonical registry schema, admin API for customer overrides (aliases), and migration UX in Console.
3) Runtime adaptor (3 weeks): implement translation layer in request path (implemented as an optional middleware). Keep CPU/latency low by caching compiled translators and using fast heuristics.
4) QA & compatibility harness (1 week): run corpus of historical calls and golden mappings; build e2e test suite.
5) Gradual rollout (2 weeks): opt-in flag per-organization, telemetry dashboard, then default-on for non-enterprise with rollback hooks.

Trade-offs:
- Latency: translation adds CPU; design must cap extra p95 latency to <= 5ms by caching and lightweight heuristics.
- Correctness vs. safety: aggressive fuzzy mapping can silently misroute calls. We'll surface confidence and require explicit opt-in for auto-correction for orgs with high-security needs.
- Operational burden: registry requires UI and lifecycle management; avoid overfitting by preferring rule-based mapping first and customer overrides for edge cases.

Risks & mitigations:
- Privacy: mappings may reveal customer naming conventions. Store per-org mappings encrypted and restrict access.
- Model hallucination of tool names: rely on deterministic matching and blacklist hallucinated names unless admin whitelists them.
- Streaming interactions: ensure tool-call handoff semantics work with streaming outputs (see notes).

Rollout plan & metrics:
- Success metrics: reduction in tool-invocation failures by 80% for mapped customers; mapping accuracy >= 99% on the training corpus; added p95 latency < 5ms.
- Observability: metrics for mapping_confidence, translation_rate, fallback_rate, manual_override_rate.

acceptance_criteria: Canonical registry and alias API implemented and accessible via admin endpoints
Runtime harmonizer middleware integrated into request path behind feature flag
Compatibility harness executes full historical corpus with >= 99% corrected calls for mapped names (post-mapping), documented false-positive list
End-to-end latency impact <= 5ms p95 for the harmonizer middleware in canary environment
Observability: metrics and tracing for mapping_confidence, translation_delta, fallback_rate, and per-org overrides
Console UX to view and edit mappings for the canary customers
Security review completed and storage of per-org mappings encrypted via KMS
notes: Streaming interplay: when a model issues a tool call mid-stream, the runtime must buffer tool invocation until harmonizer translation completes. For low-latency streaming UX, consider a 'tool-call-intent' chunk that informs client UI while final normalized call is in-flight.
Structured outputs: ensure that translated parameter payloads maintain JSON Schema annotations so downstream tool runners can validate and produce structured results consistently.

Fallback policy: default to emitting a structured error event plus a suggested corrected signature when confidence < threshold. Allow SDKs to surface an interactive prompt to end-users for confirmation.
Migration: provide a one-time migration utility to generate recommended alias mappings from historical traffic and an export for customer review.
